summary.headline: Brigade FY26 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 7,424 crore on approval delays; FY27 pre-sales guided to at least 20% growth, aiming for INR 9,000 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 pre-sales were INR 7,424 crore, down 5% YoY, as launches slipped: 8.3 million sq ft launched against a 12 million sq ft plan, with about 3.3 million sq ft pushed into FY27 (mostly Chennai). Q4 pre-sales were INR 2,521 crore (up 44% QoQ by value) from 4 million sq ft of launches. Consolidated FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 5,909 crore with EBITDA of INR 1,638 crore (28% margin), and PAT after minority interest was INR 644 crore. Operating cash flow weakened because of higher construction spend, and management expects it to rise in line with sales growth. Management says the approval issues are largely behind it, and it has guided FY27 launches of about 11.5-12 million sq ft.

segments.name: Real Estate (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 4,002 crore (+11% YoY) with EBITDA INR 525 crore. Q4 turnover INR 1,026 crore with EBITDA INR 142 crore. Management says operating POCM margins are in the high-20s to around 30%, while reported margins are diluted by revenue recognition mix.

segments.name: Leasing (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 1,303 crore (+12% YoY) with EBITDA INR 906 crore (+18%). Q4 turnover INR 337 crore with EBITDA INR 228 crore. Split: office INR 877 crore, retail INR 220 crore, management business INR 206 crore. Normalised EBITDA margin is above 80%; facility management (about INR 200 crore a year) runs at about 15%.

segments.name: Hospitality (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 604 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA INR 207 crore. Q4 turnover INR 160 crore with EBITDA INR 60 crore. Q4 occupancy 78%, ADR up 8% QoQ, RevPAR up 13% QoQ; FY26 RevPAR +6% on ADR +7%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales: at least 20% growth over FY26, aiming for about INR 9,000 crore, conditional on current sentiment and market conditions holding.

FY27 residential launch pipeline of about 11.5-11.6 million sq ft with GDV of about INR 11,900 crore: Bengaluru 4.5 million sq ft, Chennai 3 million sq ft, Hyderabad 3 million sq ft. Launches are expected to be back-ended, with Morgan Heights Phase 1 (1 million sq ft) relaunch in Q1 FY27.

Commercial pipeline of about 10 million sq ft over FY27-FY28 with capex of about INR 6,000 crore over 4 years (INR 1,200-1,700 crore a year). About 4.5 million sq ft is targeted for FY27 and about INR 800 crore of rent is expected from it and ongoing projects; leasing aimed at least at double FY26 levels.
Operating cash flow expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.
Debt-equity expected to stay well below 1x even as commercial debt rises; residential capex is self-funded, and commercial capex is a mix of debt and cash flow.
capex_capacity: Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which residential is about 75%; focus on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.
FY26 launches: 8.3 million sq ft (GDV about INR 10,000 crore) vs plan of 12 million sq ft. Q4 launches: 4 million sq ft (GDV about INR 4,500 crore).

Launch timing: Hyderabad 2 million sq ft Kokapet plot in Q3 and 1 million sq ft Northern Hyderabad project in Q4; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3 (including East Bengaluru OMR in Q3); Chennai Morgan Heights relaunch in Q1 FY27 plus two projects in Q3 and Q4. North Bengaluru project is delayed by bylaw changes requiring redesign.

Office: Whitefield JV with Bain (50:50, pure equity partners) on 10.8 acres opposite ITPL, with about 2 million sq ft of office and a 250-key 5-star hotel, targeted for completion in about 40 months after approval. Leasing: about 3 million sq ft of new completions expected in FY27. WTC Bengaluru: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft, with about 100,000 sq ft already leased.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales mix FY26: sustenance 57%, launches 43%. Q4 launch share of pre-sales about 55%. Geographic split (Q4 and FY26 approx. same): Bengaluru 65%, Hyderabad 20%, Chennai 15%.
Conversion of site visits steady at 10-12% across cities; NRI buyers around 10% of pre-sales value; some markets showing longer conversion cycles.

FY26 average realisation up 9% YoY to INR 12,107 per sq ft. Like-for-like price increase high single digits (8-9%); management plans 7-9% annual price increases after launch. Upcoming launch APR around INR 10,000 per sq ft vs inventory above INR 12,000 per sq ft; overall APR increase of 13% was partly mix-driven.

Ticket-size mix: ultra-luxury about 30% of portfolio, expected to decline. Most FY27 launch tickets below INR 3 crore; affordable up to INR 75 lakh, mid-segment up to INR 1.5 crore, premium up to INR 3 crore.
Unsold inventory about 7.5 million sq ft. Residential buyer base: GCC and IT are the largest; IT services about 26% of leasing portfolio.

Leasing: about 1.1 million sq ft leased in FY26; GCCs 58% of the lease book; top anchor tenants (above 1 lakh sq ft) are 65% of the portfolio. Lease rent escalation expected at 10-15% for Amazon's vacated space at WTC Bengaluru. Rental collections 99%.
Commercial monetisation (strata sales) annual run-rate about INR 550 crore; Twin Towers to be exited in FY27, keeping about 100,000 sq ft of common amenities.
Hospitality demand anchored in domestic travel; foreign arrivals and MICE were hit by Middle East tensions.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to fill WTC Bengaluru after Amazon exit, and expected rental uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft; about 100,000 sq ft already leased on a couple of floors. Leasing is expected floor-wise or 2-3 floors at a time over the next couple of quarters, with 10-15% rent mark-to-market (up to 20% for half-floors).

qa_highlights.name: Cumulative GDV available for launch over two years and land replenishment?
qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative GDV available for launch over the next two years, and what is the land replenishment strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling four-quarter pipeline of 11.5 million sq ft and INR 11,900-12,000 crore GDV. Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which about 75% is residential. Replenishment focused on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 9,000 crore pre-sales guidance conservative given unsold inventory and launch conversion history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted it is somewhat conservative. It cited Chennai launches selling more evenly across construction, and launch slippage into H2 leaving less time to sell in-year. Management aims to push inventory sales and pull launches forward.

qa_highlights.question: Quarter-wise launch phasing and approval status for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad about 1 million sq ft in Q3 and another 1 million in Q4; Morgan Heights 1 million sq ft relaunch in Q1; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3. The primary approval issues are considered resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow trajectory and collections trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections were flat as launches were deferred early in FY26; that cash is now converting. Operating cash flow is expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.

qa_highlights.question: Reported margin weakness in resi and leasing, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Resi reported margins reflect completion-based recognition of older, earlier-sold projects that did not capture recent price increases; POCM operating margin is around 30%. Leasing is above 80% on a normalised basis; reported margins are diluted by about INR 200 crore of facility management revenue at about 15% and about INR 35 crore of fit-out recoveries, plus a Q4 accounting gross-up.

risks_watch: FY27 pre-sales target of at least 20% growth (aiming for about INR 9,000 crore) depends on current sentiment holding; management flagged Middle East tensions and AI-related macro uncertainty.

Launch timing is back-ended: most FY27 launches fall in H2, and management said slippage into H2 leaves less time to sell in-year. North Bengaluru project is delayed by bylaw changes requiring redesign; new Bengaluru JDA may not launch this year.
Morgan Heights Phase 1 (1 million sq ft) relaunch in Q1 FY27 follows a regulatory pause; execution of this relaunch is a near-term test.

Operating cash flow recovery depends on launch conversion into collections; FY26 operating cash flow of INR 1,411 crore moderated on higher construction spend (about 4.5 million sq ft more under construction).

Commercial pipeline of about 10 million sq ft with capex of about INR 6,000 crore over 4 years; leasing of about 3 million sq ft of new completions in FY27 and WTC Bengaluru re-leasing (about 630,000 sq ft vacated by Amazon, about 100,000 sq ft leased) are key to rental growth; about INR 800 crore rent is only partly quantified (balance 5.5 million sq ft pending).

Reported margins for residential and leasing stay diluted by completion-based revenue recognition, facility management revenue at about 15% margin and fit-out recoveries; watch whether reported margins converge toward POCM levels in FY27. Twin Towers exit and strata sale run-rate (about INR 550 crore) may fall as commercial holdings change.
key_quotes: This was primarily on account of delays in obtaining approvals, with many project launches pushed to the latter half of Q4 and some moving into FY 27.

If the current sentiment and market conditions hold up, our outlook is that demand on ground will support a pre -sales outlook of at least 20% growth on our FY '26 numbers and aiming for INR9,000 crores.
So far, it's been around 30% and it will come down a little bit over the next financial year in terms of mix.
So, I think the primary issues of approvals are now behind us.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and approvals, saying the primary approval issues are behind it and the core-market fundamentals remain intact. It was cautious on timing, repeatedly flagging that launches will be back-ended into H2 and that FY27 pre-sales guidance is conditional on sentiment and market conditions holding; it called the INR 9,000 crore target "a little conservative" when pressed.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 residential pre-sales of at least 20% growth (aiming for INR 9,000 crore) on 11.6 mn sq ft of launches with INR 11,900 crore GDV, with named Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad projects and timings, though launches are back-ended and conditional on market sentiment; leasing to at least double FY26 and commercial launches of 4.5 mn sq ft are also guided.
